description: Hides the Figura avatars you are not looking at, so a crowd stops eating your frame rate

mods.name: Figura Performance
mods.description: Decides how many Figura avatars are worth showing at once. Figura draws every avatar around you in full, however far away that player is and whether or not they are on screen, and the cost is not only the model: for each of them it also edits the vanilla player model, walks its own layers and draws a custom nameplate. This mod hides the ones you are not looking at, the ones past a distance and the ones over a limit, so a crowd stops eating your frame rate. Hidden avatars cost nothing at all, the same as Figura's panic button, only per player instead of all at once. Comes with an overlay naming the avatars that cost the most, in milliseconds and frames.

releases.notes:
Avatars stop breaking, and reloading them no longer needs Figura's popup menu.

- **Reload all avatars.** A button in the settings, under General, and a key reload every player's avatar at once. Another key reloads the avatar you are looking at. Both keys are unbound by default. An avatar loaded from your wardrobe stays.
- **Hidden avatars no longer break.** Figura sends an avatar its setup event once, when the player first shows up, and that is usually while the avatar is still hidden: too far, over the limit or off screen. The mod swallowed it along with everything else, and the avatar threw script errors the moment it came into view. Now only the per tick and per frame events are skipped, each after its first run.
- **Figura's own texture bug.** When someone swaps their avatar, Figura 0.1.5 throws the old one away off the render thread, fails halfway through and leaves the avatar without textures. The mod moves that cleanup to the render thread. This also ends the "Image is not allocated" errors on resource reload that followed it.

Minecraft 1.21.6–1.21.8, Fabric.

mods.name: Figura Performance
mods.description: Puts a budget on what Figura does. Figura ticks the scripts of every loaded avatar, applies every animation and rebuilds every model tree on every single frame, no matter how far away that player is or whether they are on screen at all – which is why a crowd of avatars costs so much. This mod decides how much each avatar is worth: distant ones keep their model but lose their scripts, the far ones drop out entirely, and an adaptive mode holds a frame rate target on its own. Comes with an overlay that names the avatars eating your frame.

releases.notes:
Rewritten around what the measurements actually showed.

**Hiding, not trimming.** An avatar costs far more than its model: for every player with one, Figura also edits the vanilla player model, walks its own layers and draws a custom nameplate, all hanging off a single lookup. Cutting the model down leaves that running. Hiding the avatar fails the lookup and costs nothing at all – on a live server with thirteen people, 100 frames became 135, where the panic button gave 143.

Gone, because they broke how avatars looked and saved nothing measurable:

- script thinning ("scripts every N ticks")
- animation thinning ("animation every N frames")
- soft level of detail and its complexity floor

**Profiles gone.** One count covers both cases by itself: with two people around, a limit of twelve hides nobody, and adaptive mode reads the real frame rate instead of guessing from how many players are nearby. Two settings replace sixteen.

**Overlay** now names who is hidden, alongside the cost of each avatar in milliseconds and frames.

Minecraft 1.21.8, Fabric. Needs Fabric API and Figura. Cloth Config and Mod Menu are optional.

mods.description: Puts a budget on what Figura does. Figura ticks the scripts of every loaded avatar, applies every animation and rebuilds every model tree on every single frame, no matter how far away that player is or whether they are on screen at all – which is why a crowd of avatars costs so much. This mod decides how much each avatar is worth: distant ones keep their model but lose their scripts, the far ones drop out entirely, and an adaptive mode holds a frame rate target on its own. Comes with an overlay that names the avatars eating your frame.

releases.notes:
Fixes a bug of this mod's own making.

Cancelling `Avatar#render` for a cut down avatar also cancelled the complexity counter reset Figura does there every frame, so the complexity shown for that avatar climbed without bound (millions) and its per frame complexity budget stopped being refreshed. Cancelling `tick` skipped the permission, sound and particle bookkeeping in the same way.

Everything now hangs off `Avatar#run`, the one method every Lua event goes through: cut down avatars skip the per frame events and thin the per tick ones, while Figura's own accounting runs untouched. Pings, input and chat events are never skipped unless the avatar is off entirely, so things like a scripted costume change still come through.

The wrong numbers were only ever reported, never stored – restarting the game clears them.
